repository.name: @webex/internal-plugin-encryption
repository.purpose: Internal plugin registered as webex.internal.encryption that encrypts and decrypts Webex content with keys held by the Key Management Service (KMS). Encryption wraps text and binary data as JWE and files as SCRs, fetches each key from KMS once, and caches it, private key material included, in the SDK unbounded storage. Its child webex.internal.encryption.kms negotiates an ECDH session with KMS, wraps every KMS request (resources, authorizations, unbound keys, customer master keys), batches the requests to the encryption service, and matches the responses that arrive as Mercury encryption.kms_message events. Before negotiating, it validates the KMS static key: the mandatory key checks always run, and certificate-chain trust is checked only when shouldValidateKMSCertificate is true, against configured roots or the signed Cisco Union bundle shipped in assets/. Optional report-only checks only emit metrics. Registered payload transforms wrap outbound kmsMessage bodies, unwrap inbound ones, and turn DRY error responses into DryError. KMS failures reject with KmsError, KmsTimeoutError, or KMSError.

internal-plugin-encryption-sdk.summary: Published npm package (internal plugin). main is dist/index.js and devMain is src/index.js; the browser field swaps caroots-asset and ensure-buffer for browser builds; no type declarations are published. Importing it imports @webex/internal-plugin-device and @webex/internal-plugin-mercury and registers Encryption as internal plugin 'encryption' with its config, three payload predicates and transforms (encryptKmsMessage, decryptKmsMessage, decryptErrorResponse), and, only when NODE_ENV is test, KmsDryErrorInterceptor. The entry exports the default Encryption, KMS, KmsError, and DryError. webex.internal.encryption exposes encryptText, decryptText, encryptBinaryData, decryptBinaryData, encryptScr, decryptScr, encryptBinary, decryptBinary, download, getKey, and processKmsMessageEvent; webex.internal.encryption.kms exposes the KMS request methods; config lives under webex.config.encryption. Specified in src/docs/README.md.

encryption-key-cache-entry.summary: getKey stores each fetched key in the plugin's unbounded storage (webex-core plugin store, namespace Encryption) under the key URI, or under the key URI plus /onBehalfOf/ plus a user id, as JSON.stringify of the KMS key object with its JWK serialized by toJSON(true), so private key material is included. No version field, TTL, or eviction exists; an unreadable entry is replaced by a fresh KMS fetch.

encryption-kms-events.summary: webex.internal.encryption triggers event:kms:key:revoke:encryption:failure when a KMS response item has status 405 and errorCode 405005 or 405006 (src/constants.js, src/kms-batcher.js). src/kms.js triggers client:InvalidRequestError on the webex instance when a request fails with KMSError. No in-repository source listens for either event.

kms-encryption-service-http.source: Webex encryption service (catalog service name encryption; route definitions are not in this repository)
kms-encryption-service-http.summary: GET kms/<userId> answers {kmsCluster, rsaPublicKey}, where rsaPublicKey is a JSON string holding the KMS static JWK (kid, kty, n, e, x5c). POST kms/messages takes {destination: kmsCluster, kmsMessages: [wrapped JWE]}; its HTTP response is ignored, and each KMS response arrives later over Mercury.

mercury-kms-message-events.source: @webex/internal-plugin-mercury (workspace package; module spec consulted: packages/@webex/internal-plugin-mercury/src/docs/README.md, autowiring rule; code consulted: src/mercury.js)
mercury-kms-message-events.summary: Mercury routes an envelope whose data.eventType is encryption.kms_message to webex.internal.encryption.processKmsMessageEvent(data), where data.encryption.kmsMessages holds the wrapped responses; handler errors are logged by Mercury and not rethrown. mercury.connect() resolves at once when connected, joins an in-flight connect, and registers the device first. The mercury spec is stale on its multi-session API, which this package does not use.

node-kms-message-format.source: node-kms npm package (^0.4.1 in package.json; not in this repository)
node-kms-message-format.summary: Context (clientInfo, serverInfo, ephemeralKey, createECDHKey, deriveEphemeralKey), Request (wrap with serverKey for the ECDHE request), and Response (unwrap). The KMS JSON request bodies (method, uri, and fields) are wrapped as compact JWE by this library.

cisco-union-bundle.summary: Cisco Trusted Root Store Union bundle, a CMS-signed .p7b shipped as assets/ios_union-<version>.p7b and copied to dist/assets by build:assets. src/union-bundle.js (generated by scripts/refresh-union-bundle.js) names the file and sets the rollback floor UNION_BUNDLE_VERSION; the default config loads it from assetsBaseUrl (getUmdAssetsBaseUrl) or, in Node, from the packaged copy.

kms-caroots-verifier.source: @webex/kms-caroots (workspace package; no spec exists; code consulted: packages/@webex/kms-caroots/verify.js and index.js)
kms-caroots-verifier.summary: verifyUnionBundle(bytes, {crypto, minBundleVersion}) resolves {caroots, bundleName, bundleVersion, signingTime} after checking the CMS signature against the pinned TRS bundle root, or rejects with UnionBundleVerificationError whose reason is parse, signature, attributes, name, version, signing-time, or no-certificates. loadUnionBundle({input}) exists only in the Node entry and is used by scripts/refresh-union-bundle.js.

webex-core-plugin-host.source: @webex/webex-core (workspace package; module spec consulted: packages/@webex/webex-core/src/docs/README.md MOD-008, MOD-016, MOD-027, MOD-037, MOD-044, MOD-048, UC-004)
webex-core-plugin-host.summary: registerInternalPlugin merges config and concatenates payloadTransformer predicates and transforms; transform runs predicates by direction (outbound on requests, inbound on responses and on response errors, which then still reject); WebexPlugin gives logger, request, and config from webex.config[namespace lowercased]; interceptor create functions run with this bound to the webex instance; webex.request with service and resource goes through the interceptor chain and rejects with WebexHttpError.

webex-core-batcher.source: @webex/webex-core Batcher (module spec consulted: packages/@webex/webex-core/src/docs/README.md MOD-050 to MOD-053)
webex-core-batcher.summary: Batcher.request runs fingerprintRequest, prepareItem, enqueue, and a capped debounce driven by batcherWait, batcherMaxCalls, and batcherMaxWait from the subclass namespace config; executeQueue sends up to batcherMaxCalls items through prepareRequest and submitHttpRequest; acceptItem routes each response through didItemFail to handleItemSuccess or handleItemFailure; a flush failure is fanned out and never thrown.

webex-core-static-asset-loader.source: @webex/webex-core StaticAssetLoader (no webex-core spec covers it; code consulted: packages/@webex/webex-core/src/lib/static-asset-loader.ts)
webex-core-static-asset-loader.summary: new StaticAssetLoader({baseUrl}, {parent: webex}).getBytes(name) GETs the asset as a buffer without the auth header, tracking id, user agent, or redirect header, rejects a non-2xx, HTML, or non-binary response, caches one promise per URL with eviction on failure, and resolves a fresh Uint8Array. When services.validateCatalogUrls is true, the catalog URL interceptor rejects asset hosts that are not in allowedDomains.

webex-core-storage.summary: WebexPlugin.unboundedStorage get rejects NotFoundError for a missing key; put serializes and stores the value; where it persists depends on the host's unbounded storage adapter.

common-utilities.source: @webex/common and @webex/common-timers (module specs consulted: packages/@webex/common/src/docs/README.md MOD-002, MOD-003, MOD-005; packages/@webex/common-timers/src/docs/README.md MOD-001, MOD-002)
common-utilities.summary: oneFlight shares one in-flight promise per method and key on an instance and evicts it when it settles; tap passes the value through after awaiting the callback's promise; proxyEvents and transferEvents forward progress events; Exception builds the message from parse; isBuffer; getUmdAssetsBaseUrl picks the development path, the webex UMD assets on unpkg, the plugin dist assets on unpkg, or the page-relative path; safeSetTimeout forwards to setTimeout and unrefs the timer.

internal-plugin-device-registration.source: @webex/internal-plugin-device (workspace package; module spec consulted: packages/@webex/internal-plugin-device/src/docs/README.md MOD-001, MOD-012)
internal-plugin-device-registration.summary: Importing the package registers internal plugin device; webex.internal.device.userId and url are set from the WDM registration body and read here for the KMS details request and the KMS client identity.

internal-plugin-metrics-client-metrics.source: @webex/internal-plugin-metrics (workspace package, not declared in package.json; module spec consulted: packages/@webex/internal-plugin-metrics/src/docs/README.md MOD-008)
internal-plugin-metrics-client-metrics.summary: webex.internal.metrics.submitClientMetrics(name, payload) returns the batcher promise and throws synchronously for a missing name. This package assumes the plugin is registered by the host and guards both the throw and the rejection.

files-download-endpoints-http.source: Webex files service (reached on the host of the caller's file URL; route definitions are not in this repository)
files-download-endpoints-http.summary: POST https://<file host>/v1/download/endpoints with {endpoints: [fileUrl], allow?} answers {endpoints: {fileUrl: downloadUrl}}; the encrypted bytes are then fetched with GET from the returned URL.
